Detailed method

Sourdough pizzas. Currently 500 g flour, 70% hydration, 20% starter, 2.5% salt, and 0% yeast. That is 350 g water, 100 g starter, 12.5 g salt, 962.5 g of dough. The starter is itself 100% hydration, the same assumption used for effective hydration. The page shows 72.7% effective hydration. Currently 5 balls of 192.5 g each. Sauce, cheese, and other toppings are extra and are not in the gram total. These times assume you only change the flour amount and keep the percentages the same. Still judge the dough by how it looks and feels.

  1. Starter Use 100 g of starter that is bubbly and has about doubled. That starter is part of the gram total.
  2. Mix Stir 500 g flour, 350 g water, the 100 g starter and 12.5 g salt until no dry flour remains. At 70% the dough is soft. Aim for about 24°C (75°F).
  3. Bulk Cover it at about 24°C (75°F) for about 2 hours and fold it twice. Then refrigerate the covered dough at about 4°C (39°F) for 12 to 24 hours. It should grow by about half, not spill over.
  4. Shape Divide the 962.5 g into 5 pieces of 192.5 g each and tighten each piece into a ball. The default 962.5 g uses a baking stone or tray about 40 cm across. If you change the amount, use a stone sized to fit, or bake in batches.
  5. Warm Take the dough out 60 to 90 minutes before baking. Stretch each ball by hand on a floured peel. Leave a rim and a thin center.
  6. Bake Heat the oven to 250°C (480°F) with a stone or steel for 45 minutes. Add sauce and cheese if you want them. Those toppings are extra and are not in the gram total. Bake 7 to 10 minutes, until the rim is spotted and the center is set. Rest 2 minutes before you cut.
